title: Transported finite étale trace section formula
statement: Let f:Y→X and g:X′→X be étale morphisms, F an abelian sheaf on X, and τ:f_*f⁻¹F→F satisfy the local sum predicate [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-local-sums]. Set f′:Y×_XX′→X′ and F′=g⁻¹F. Write ρ for the inverse-image restriction isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. For any W in X′_Et and any pasting isomorphism κ_W:B_f′W≅B_fW over X with the specified projections to W and Y [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting], transport the τ component to F′(W) using ρ at B_f′W, F(κ_W⁻¹), and ρ_W⁻¹. For each input s∈F′(B_f′W), each h:T→W, and each finite clopen splitting i_j:V_j→B_f′T with inverse t_j to the projection to T, restriction along h of this transported section equals the sum over j of restriction along t_j≫i_j of F′(B_f′h)(s). The index set may be empty. No finiteness of f and no trace on X′ are assumed.

source.place: Section 03SH, paragraph after Definition 03SE; SGA 4, Exposé IX, 5.1

proof.text: Construct the canonical pullback pasting isomorphism explicitly using pullback.lift and prove its inverse equations with pullback.hom_ext. Transport the supplied cofan through this isomorphism; preserve its inverse equations and open/closed immersion properties by composition with the isomorphism. Apply FiniteEtaleTraceLocalSums to the transported splitting. The supplied projection identities at W imply compatibility with the pullback maps induced by h. Naturality of the restriction isomorphism and of the composite of the trace with the restriction inverse moves restriction along h to T. Cancel the pasting isomorphism and the restriction isomorphism in each summand, distribute composition over the finite sum, and evaluate on s. This also works for an empty index type.
